summary.intent: Run the GSD plan-phase workflow for CipherBox phase 68.2 (SDK-owned read chain and resolved folder listings), then execute all resulting plans wave-by-wave, while also spinning up a parallel worktree to begin phase 69 independently.
summary.outcome: Phase 68.2 was fully planned (research, Nyquist validation, D-07 scope decision, pattern mapping, 12 plans across 7 waves) and passed plan-checker verification with 2 non-blocking warnings; execution began sequentially on the main tree, with Wave 1 (SDK read-path ROT-07 gate) completed and independently spot-checked, and Wave 2 dispatched. A separate git worktree for phase 69 was created off origin/main for parallel work.

repo: gsd-tools query commit often reports `commit_failed` even when the commit actually lands in git log — a known false-negative, always verify with `git log` before treating it as a real failure.

The plan-phase workflow's UI capability gate only blocks if a UI hook is actually active in `activeHooks`; a `block:true` from the lower-level `ui-plan-gate` check is irrelevant if no UI hook fired for the phase.
Intel API-surface extraction (§7.9) can return 0 symbols for this monorepo and should be omitted from planner prompts as noise rather than passed through.
Schema-gate planner contribution should be skipped when a phase touches zero ORM/DB schema files (e.g., pure SDK/codec/web work).

worktree.baseRef must be checked before dispatching executors into worktrees — if it defaults to 'fresh' (origin/main) instead of 'head', executors would miss uncommitted-to-main planning commits (like PLAN.md files) on the phase branch.

In this pnpm monorepo, worktree-based parallel execution requires a fresh `pnpm install` per worktree, which is expensive; for phases with mostly single-plan waves, sequential execution on the main tree is more robust and avoids that cost.

REQUIREMENTS.md registration (new requirement IDs like SDK-READ-01..04) must happen before the planner runs so coverage gates have a stable target — done via three edits: requirement section, traceability rows, coverage summary.

code.finding: RotationHighWater.enforceResolved gate added at root resolve site (resolvePublishedNode) as part of closing the zero-gating read-path security gap (ROT-07).
enforceResolved gate also added in dfsFindFolder's child loop, alongside pre-existing write-path gate at line 1156.
New TDD RED->GREEN test file verifying the anti-rollback read-path gate; independently re-run and confirmed 296/296 passing.

workflow: For strictly sequential workflows (research feeding Nyquist VALIDATION.md and the planner), spawn subagents synchronously and wait rather than parallelizing.
Before advancing past a security-critical wave, independently re-run acceptance tests rather than trusting the executor's self-reported summary.

When a genuine scope ambiguity is surfaced by research (e.g., D-07's literal wording sweeping in extra files), pause with AskUserQuestion and then lock the resolution into CONTEXT.md so the planner treats it as decided.
Use plain `git worktree add` (not EnterWorktree) when the orchestrator needs to keep driving work in the current checkout while a separate worktree handles independent parallel work.
Even with auto_advance:true, pause for confirmation before launching a large (12-plan, 7-wave) execution of security-critical code, especially when checker warnings exist.

friction: gsd-tools commit helper returned false 'commit_failed' results multiple times, requiring manual git log verification each time to confirm commits actually landed.
git fetch failed from the sandboxed session (no network access to GitHub), forcing reliance on the last-known local origin/main ref for the phase-69 worktree base.
Gap-analysis parser choked on control characters in the 'rendered' field output, requiring a fallback to running the check directly.
Two non-blocking plan-checker warnings surfaced about D-03's poll-invalidation leg lacking dedicated automated test coverage (only grep-based verification).
